title: Biodegradable Stents in the Treatment of Arterial Stenosis
content:
Arterial diseases (AD) are a major health problem with high mortality and morbidity. Endovascular interventions, including balloon angioplasty (BA), bare-metal stent (BMS), drug-eluting stents (DES) and drug-coated balloons (DCB), have provided significant progress in their treatments. However, the problem has not been fully solved, particularly restenosis remains a major issue. In this context, bioresorbable vascular stents (BVSs) have been a promising investigation topic. The articles that evaluate BVSs were included in this traditional review manuscript. Studies have shown that challenges remain, such as negative vascular remodeling and elastic recoil after angioplasty, stent-related injury and in-stent restenosis after BMS. Although DESs have reduced these problems to an important extent, the durable stent structures cannot prevent late stent thrombosis, and delay arterial recovery. BVSs have lower support strength and tend to have thicker scaffold, increasing the risk of scaffold thrombosis.
Although the study results are inconsistent, the superiority of BVS over DES has not been demonstrated in randomized trials, and DES devices are still the first choice for most arterial disease cases. Esprit BTK (Abbott Vascular) was approved by the US FDA for use in below-knee lesions in 2024, which may be a promising light for the use of BVS in other vascular events. Improving the scaffold design and thickness of BVSs may offer a new pathway. Large-scale and longer-follow-up comparative studies are still needed.
The article aims to provide an overview of the use of biodegradable stents in the endovascular treatment of vascular stenosis.
